title: OOM handoff: operator / driver mismatch scratchpad
body:
Topline: quick scratchpad while pairing with ops - running into intermittent OOMs on a node after a rolling upgrade of the GPU operator and host drivers. Symptoms are low-frequency but high-impact; repro window ~1-2 hours after node boot or pod restart.

Recent context:
- K8s cluster: 1.29.x, custom GPU node image that includes driver 535.86.05 (packaged).
- GPU operator upgrade from v1.14 -> v1.15 bumped nvidia-container-toolkit and changed runc config (runc hooks).
- Affected service: tokenized-generation pods (llm-serving). Heavy KV cache usage (large context >32k).

Observed behavior summary:
- Pod running load test (batching enabled) crashes with process OOM (container exit) and node dmesg shows driver reprobe/killing of process-related GPU memory hints.
- Error in pod logs right before crash: "CUDA error: unspecified launch failure (code 999)" and sometimes "CUDA driver version is insufficient for runtime" on restart.
- nvidia-smi intermittently reports "No running processes found" then shortly after shows application PID but memory zero.

Commands tried + raw outputs (captured during a repro):
1) nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
---- snip ----
GPU 0:
  FB Memory Usage
    Total                      : 49152 MiB
    Used                       : 12288 MiB
    Free                       : 36864 MiB
---- end snip ----

2) dmesg | tail -n 120  (relevant lines)
[k] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[k] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 13, PID=22514 GPU has fallen off the bus
[k] audit: type=1400 audit(1700000000.000:123): apparmor="DENIED" operation="capable" pid=1 comm="containerd" capability=16

3) docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.2-runtime nvidia-smi
Output: "NVRM: The NVIDIA kernel module has changed; please reboot the system to use the new module."

4) ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so
Output (notes):	libnvidia-ml.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 (0x00007f...)

5) readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1.0.0 (mismatch across nodes seen)

6) ps aux | grep -E "nvidia|cuda" -> shows both host-driver processes and container shim processes.

7) strace -f -e openat -p <pid of crashed process> (attempted) - mostly failed because process dies too quickly; caught ENOENT on /etc/nvidia/gridd.conf and missing /run/nvidia/driver.sock once in one node.

Hypothesis thread:
- Hypothesis A: Operator upgrade left mixed libcuda versions on host (some symlinks pointing to older libcuda) + container nvidia libs bundled -> rpath/LD_PRELOAD interactions cause the container runtime to load host libcuda that doesn't match loaded kernel module. This leads to transient "driver version insufficient" messages and XIDs.
- Hypothesis B: The new operator changed cgroup or runc hook ordering which delays nv-hostengine setup causing initial allocations to fail (race at pod start). After resume, kernel reports GPU "fall off bus" during memory reclamation.
- Hypothesis C: Memory fragmentation + KVcache large allocations push the driver into a state where async-diagnostic XID 13 is triggered (failed GPU page faults under stress).

Notes about heterogeneity found:
- Node-a: kernel 6.1.45 + driver 535.86.05 (package-installed).
- Node-b: kernel 6.6.9 + driver 525.x (legacy packaged); both in same nodepool label.
- Container image contains CUDA 12.2 libs (libcuda stubs) which are ABI compatible but not always driver compatible if host has older kernel driver.

Repro / minimal test I'm keeping in parallel:
- Run a small cuda-samples vectorAdd loop in the same serving image, spawn 10 threads allocating 2GiB each via cudaMalloc, loop to free/alloc and check for XID or segfault. Use watch -n1 nvidia-smi to correlate. Repro script: 
  - docker run --gpus all --rm -v $(pwd):/src test-serve-image /bin/bash -c "/src/repro.sh"
- repro.sh is simple: compile nvcc vectorAdd and run in a loop with env CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get deterministic failures.

Quick patches tried locally (cluster-level):
- Reboot node (temporarily resolved; no OOMs for ~4h).
- Forced reinstall driver 535.86.05 on nodes (consistently stable on node-a but node-b still exhibited XID 13).
- Set env in pod: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-allocator.so (experimental) -> pod fails to start sometimes with load errors.
- Changed nvidia-container-runtime config to prefer host-provided libraries (nvidia-container-cli --load-kmods) -> mixed results, some pods failed to start with "module not found".

Next investigative steps (TODO):
- Add pre-start hook in serving pods to run: ldd $(which python) | grep libcuda and readlink -f those libs; log to pod /tmp/debug-libs.txt. This helps validate whether container is getting host lib or image lib.
- Force node-pool rolling with consistent driver (choose driver 535.x only) and monitor latency and OOM rate for 48h.
- Reproduce with simplified workload to get deterministic XID (vectorAdd loop). Enable persistence-mode and set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to produce synchronous faults.
- Collect full /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and /var/log/kern.log on any node that produces GPU has fallen off the bus.
- Add a brief wrapper to the serving binary to call cuInit(0) on start and catch driver version from cudaDriverGetVersion() and cudaRuntimeGetVersion() and log both. This will quickly show mismatch patterns in logs.

Notes / heuristics from prior hunts:
- If you see "NVRM: The NVIDIA kernel module has changed; please reboot the system to use the new module" it usually indicates leftover module state after dpkg/apt install or driver update without reboot. Rebooting fixes but doesn't explain why some nodes spontaneously fail later.
- Xid 13 often indicates a PCIe xfer fault or GPU page fault under heavy memory churn; check for firmware versions mismatch too.
- libcuda symlink differences across nodes have bitten us before when operator updated container-toolkit and host lib packaging changed naming conventions.

Notes-to-self: when pairing with ops tomorrow, ask them to verify the node image build step - ensure native driver for kernel is baked in, not installed at runtime. Also ask about node auto-upgrade windows.

Quick copy of environment variables seen inside a crash pod (sanitized):
- CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
- NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility,video
- NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA=cuda>=12.0

Final: this doc is a live scratchpad. Will paste key logs to JIRA-ENG-1427 and attach the collected ldd outputs. Keep short notes here rather than modifying Confluence until we lock a root cause.

---
Recent additions (2026-03-12):
- Captured driver version from inside pod (via cudaDriverGetVersion): 53500 (reported), cudaRuntimeGetVersion: 12020. Some nodes reported driver 52500 inside pod although host had 535 package present -> indicates containers loading different libcuda (stubs vs host).
- Action: temporarily set NODE_LABEL gpu-driver=535 and drain other nodes. Observing 72h no-corruption on the drained pool so far.

End of scratchpad.
